    1. SysMLinJavaUnits()

Class SysMLinJavaUnits

java.lang.Object
sysmlinjava.common.SysMLAnything
sysmlinjava.units.SysMLUnitsCollection
sysmlinjava.units.SysMLinJavaUnits
public class SysMLinJavaUnits extends SysMLUnitsCollection
SysMLinJava represention of SysML's prescribed units and supplementary units. Included are the SI standard units prescribed by the SysML standard, as well as a number of additional units useful for SysMLinJava modeling. Individual instances of SysMLUnit are self described by their individual field values, i.e. name, symbol, description, definitionURI, and quantityKind.

Each SysMLUnit instance is a static final instance, i.e. the units declared here must be used as is. If different or additional units are needed, they should be instantiated in a new class that extends the SysMLUnits class similar to this class. For example, to create a new unit outside of the unit collection in this SysMLinJavaUnits class, simply instantiate the SysMLUnit for the new unit in an extending class as follows: 

public class MySysMLUnits extends SysMLUnitsCollection
{
           :
        @Unit
        public static final SysMLUnit MyNewUnit = new SysMLUnit("newUnit", "nu", "My new unit description", "http://adomain.com/units", Optional.of(SysMLQuantityKinds.Each));
           :
}
References to the new unit would then be as follows: 
   public class MyAttributeType extends SysMLAttributeType
   {
           :
       @Override
       protected void createUnits()
       {
           units = MySysMLUnits.MyNewUnit;
       }
           :
   }
Note that the SI units can be identified by their definitionURI argument in their constructors. This argument for SI units contains the link to the "NIST Special Publication 330" for the SI units.

ModelerOne
